TIL: The first 16 US Presidents represented 6 different political parties, where the final 31 Presidents only represented 2.
Before you freak out on my math, there is an overlap in the data between Franklin Pierce and Abraham Lincoln,

Well duh. Those two were built out of mergers of the original 16.

EDIT: Let me explain.

Washington switched to Federalist during his second term, so he doesn't count.

The first few elections post-Washington were still two-party elections, with the Federalists being one and the Democratic-Republicans being the other.

The Federalists then fell apart, and former Federalist sympathizers formed the Democratic party. Somewhere before that, the Democratic-Republicans renamed themselves to simply the Republicans. There's parties #4 and #6.

The Whigs sprouted up after the collapse of the Republicans as a way of reviving Republican styles of thought, and for all intents and purposes can be seen as a 'successor' to the original Republican party. In the wake of King Andrew I's failed attempt at re-election, the Whigs fused with a few other Anti-Jacksonians to form the pre-New Deal Republican Party (modern-day Democrats).

 

The only political party in American history that ever had any relevance and wasn't directly succeeding or preceding some other party would be the Populist Party in the late 1800s, and they just annexed themselves into the Democratic Party once they realized that third-parties don't get votes.
